etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English remote, from Old French remot, masculine, remote, feminine, from Latin remotus, past participle of removere (“to remove”), from re- + movere (“to move”).

definitions.definition: (broadcasting) An element of broadcast programming originating away from the station's or show's control room.
(computing) A source control repository hosted on a remote machine, rather than locally.
(computing) To connect to a computer from a remote location.

quote.citation: 2010, Bill English, Microsoft Sharepoint 2010: Administrator's Companion:
quote.text: These requirements are applicable whether you are remoting into a server or locally executing SharePoint cmdlets.
